dynasties.name: Nanda
dynasties.note: The start is disputed. This follows the Harvard chronology.

dynasties.name: Maurya
dynasties.note: Broad imperial period. Territorial reach changed substantially.

dynasties.name: Shunga
dynasties.note: Follows the Harvard date range. Other chronologies place the start at 185 BCE.

dynasties.name: Kushan
dynasties.note: Start follows Kujula Kadphises in the ruler list. The approximate end follows the dynasty heading, including later rulers.

dynasties.name: Brahman dynasty of Sindh
dynasties.note: Includes successors after Dahir’s defeat in 712, following the source chronology.

dynasties.name: Ghaznavid · Punjab phase
dynasties.note: Shows the Punjab phase from the Met chronology, ending with the last Lahore ruler. Earlier Afghanistan-based rule and raids are outside this bar.

dynasties.name: Ghurid · northern rule
dynasties.note: Shows Muhammad Ghuri’s northern Indian phase from the Harvard ruler list, rather than the full Afghanistan-based dynasty.

dynasties.name: Arghun
dynasties.note: Uses the Met’s dynastic range, which includes a later period of reduced authority.

dynasties.name: Sukerchakia · Sikh Empire
dynasties.note: From the capture of Lahore to British annexation. Ranjit Singh took the title maharaja in 1801.

dynasties.name: Gupta
dynasties.note: Uses the Harvard imperial range. The dynasty’s beginnings and the survival of later branches are dated differently elsewhere.

dynasties.name: Pushyabhuti / Vardhana
dynasties.note: Begins with the first dated ruler in this source’s list and ends with Harsha. Earlier founders are undated.

dynasties.name: Chandela
dynasties.note: The bar follows the source’s dynastic range, including periods of changing autonomy.

dynasties.name: Mamluk · Delhi
dynasties.note: Groups the early slave-king lines of the Delhi Sultanate.

dynasties.name: Khalji · Delhi
dynasties.area: Delhi, northern India and Deccan campaigns

dynasties.name: Tughluq
dynasties.note: Ends with Mahmud Shah II in the Met ruler list. Authority fragmented before the end.

dynasties.name: Sur
dynasties.note: Main imperial phase ending with the Mughal restoration. Later regional resistance is not shown.

dynasties.name: Mughal
dynasties.area: Northern subcontinent, later much of the Deccan
dynasties.note: The gap marks Sur rule. Later emperors had greatly reduced power. The end follows the source’s formal abolition date of 1858, after the capture of Delhi in 1857.

dynasties.name: Sharqi
dynasties.note: Uses the Met range. Later claims beyond this period are not plotted.

dynasties.name: Nawabs of Awadh
dynasties.note: A regional ruling house with increasing British dependence, ending in annexation.

dynasties.name: Pala · Bengal
dynasties.note: Bengal includes territory in both modern Bangladesh and India.

dynasties.name: Mlechchha / Salastambha
dynasties.note: Kamarupa branch. Source polity geometry is broader than the specific family and is assigned by this chronology’s dates.

dynasties.name: Husain Shahi
dynasties.note: Dates follow the title of Momtazur Rahman Tarafdar’s study, published by the Asiatic Society of Pakistan.

dynasties.name: Vakataka
dynasties.note: The source gives mid-third to late-fifth century. Endpoints are rounded plotting anchors.

dynasties.name: Kadamba · early line
dynasties.note: Early dynasty only. Later branches are not included.

dynasties.name: Satavahana · dated phases
dynasties.note: Early and later phases follow separate Harvard lists. The gap is a gap in this selected chronology, not evidence that the dynasty ceased to exist.

dynasties.name: Chalukya · Badami
dynasties.note: The source gives early sixth century for the start. 500 is a rounded plotting anchor.

dynasties.name: Rashtrakuta
dynasties.note: Uses the Harvard dynastic range, including the last claimant after the loss of imperial power in 973.

dynasties.name: Hoysala
dynasties.note: Follows the Met chronology. Earlier family origins are outside this range.

dynasties.name: Bahmani
dynasties.note: Includes the late period when provincial successor states held much of the power.

dynasties.name: Qutb Shahi
dynasties.note: The Met begins with Sultan Quli’s governorship, earlier than the conventional independence date of 1518.

dynasties.name: Bhat Peshwas
dynasties.area: Pune and the Maratha political sphere
dynasties.note: Hereditary chief ministers who came to exercise executive power. This is not a bar for the full Maratha confederacy.

dynasties.name: Asaf Jahi
dynasties.note: From 1724 the Nizams exercised substantial practical autonomy while acknowledging nominal Mughal suzerainty. French influence shaped the succession struggles of 1748–1762. The dotted phase begins with the permanent Company subsidiary alliance of 1798, strengthened in 1800. A solid bar means before British paramountcy, not complete formal independence.

dynasties.name: Pallava · later phase
dynasties.note: Uses the later phase listed by Harvard, not the family’s earliest attestation.

dynasties.name: Pandya · early medieval
dynasties.note: Only this dated phase is shown. Ancient predecessors and the later Pandya revival are not included.

dynasties.name: Chola · imperial phase
dynasties.area: Tamil region and changing southern territories
dynasties.note: Imperial revival only. Earlier Cholas are not represented.

dynasties.name: Sena
dynasties.note: Uses the source’s dynasty heading. The ruler list also includes earlier founders and later successors, so these are approximate phase dates.

dynasties.name: Chalukya · Kalyani
dynasties.note: Uses the dynasty heading, rather than the slightly earlier accession of Taila II.

dynasties.name: Sangama · Vijayanagara
dynasties.note: Begins with Harihara I’s dated rule in the source. Earlier family origins are undated.

dynasties.name: Tuluva · Vijayanagara
dynasties.note: Begins with Vira Narasimha’s accession. The source includes Sadasiva’s nominal rule to 1576, overlapping the Aravidu line.

dynasties.name: Aravidu · Vijayanagara
dynasties.area: Southern India after the loss of Vijayanagara
dynasties.note: Uses the source’s dynasty heading. Its ruler list extends the last king’s life or claims beyond this end date.

dynasties.name: Shah Mir
dynasties.note: The gap marks Mirza Haydar Dughlat’s governorship in the source ruler list.

dynasties.name: Chak
dynasties.note: Includes the last ruler after the Mughal conquest in 1586, following the Met’s list.

dynasties.name: East India Company · territorial rule
dynasties.area: Changing British-controlled territories in the subcontinent
dynasties.note: A colonial company regime. The phase begins at Plassey, not the company’s foundation or its earlier trading settlements. Territories expanded over time.

dynasties.name: British Raj · Crown rule
dynasties.area: Changing British-controlled territories in the subcontinent
dynasties.note: British Crown administration. Provinces under direct rule and princely states under paramountcy had different relationships with it. Annual dating includes the transfer year 1947.
